turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Sure. What can I help you with?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's a good way to look at it.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Heartbreak

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You too.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Hey Jimmy, good to hear from you. How have you been doing lately?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hi George. I've been okay, I guess. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster recently.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I get that. You've had a lot on your plate. What's been going on?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Well, I went to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for the first time yesterday.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That's a huge step, Jimmy. I'm really proud of you for taking it. How did it feel?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Intimidating, honestly. Walking in there, not knowing anyone, feeling vulnerable... it wasn't easy.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I can only imagine how tough that must have been. But you did it, and that says a lot about your courage.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks, George. I kept thinking about that day at the gathering when I tried to talk to everyone but felt ignored.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I remember you mentioning that. It must've been so frustrating to feel unheard by people you consider friends.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, it was. I guess that's part of why I pushed myself to try something different, like the AA meeting.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That makes sense. It sounds like you’re finding new ways to address things that were weighing you down.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, I hope so. I just worry about the process, you know? What if I can't handle it?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It's normal to feel that way, Jimmy. Recovery is a journey, not a sprint. It's okay to have doubts.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I appreciate that. I do want to keep going, but the fear of failing is there.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Fear is natural, but remember you've already taken the first step. You have the support to go through this.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks, that helps. The people at the meeting were welcoming, which made a difference.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That's really good to hear. It's important to feel supported and understood in a group like that.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, it felt different from trying to talk with my current friends. I think I need this new beginning.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It sounds like you're on the right path, Jimmy. I'm here for you, whatever you need.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That really means a lot to me, George. Thanks for being there.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How have the AA meetings been going?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hey there. Well, surprisingly, they've been quite helpful. I met someone there, Bob, who's kind of going through the same issues.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That's great to hear. It must feel nice to have someone who truly understands what you're going through.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, definitely. It feels different from when I talked to my other friends. They just didn't get it, you know?

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I remember you mentioned feeling dismissed by them before. It sounds like finding someone who empathizes really makes a difference.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Exactly. With Bob, I don't feel judged. We can share our stories, and it's like this unspoken bond.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That unspoken understanding can be so powerful. Have you been able to open up more because of it?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: A bit. It's scary, but I’ve been sharing more of my feelings, and it feels freeing somehow. The fear of being judged or not being taken seriously is starting to fade.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds like real progress, Jimmy. Have you felt any changes in your day-to-day life since attending these meetings?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, definitely. I've started to recognize some patterns in my behavior and why I turned to alcohol. It's frightening to see, but it’s the first step, I guess.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Acknowledging those patterns is a huge step. It's brave of you to face those issues head-on.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks. I just sometimes worry if I’m too late, you know? That I might lose everything.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It's normal to feel that way, but you’re taking action now, and that’s important. It's never too late to make a change.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, you're right. I guess I just have to keep reminding myself of that.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Absolutely. And remember, you're not alone in this. Bob and others at AA are there for you, and so am I.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I appreciate that. It's comforting to have a supportive net. I need to hold onto that.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You're building a strong foundation, Jimmy. Just keep taking it one day at a time.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks. It helps to break it down like that. I’ll try to focus on each day and not get overwhelmed.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds like a solid plan. You've got this, Jimmy. Remember, progress is progress, no matter how small.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks a lot. Your words mean a lot to me right now. I’ll keep them in mind.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Anytime. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Keep me posted on how things go, okay?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I will. Thanks again, really. I'll talk to you soon.
